Boundary of use: the three scenes below are editorial fiction, used only to practise telling two kinds of evidence apart, corresponding to no real shop or person. How the work splits follows willingness, experience and duty, not type; either type can keep the books, and either can handle channels.

In this fictional cash squeeze, both partners have the same payment calendar and cash records. They can look for possible changes to the schedule and verify which payments fall due. Neither line of inquiry identifies either type.

compare_blocks.title: Illustrative scenarios

compare_blocks.body:
The three things most often used as evidence: who talks better, who likes working with their hands, whose desk is messier. All three fail. An ENFP may say nothing at an unfamiliar dinner, and an ISTP can talk about engines with a friend for two hours; an ISTP's bench can be tidy, and an ENFP's drawer can be sorted down to every cable.

The second mismatch reads difference as ability. Saying ENFP only draws pies in the sky and ISTP only turns screws turns a processing position into a level of skill. Position describes where information is more often taken up, not how well it is handled, and not who is better at deciding.

The third treats P as unreliable. Both can write a schedule clearly and deliver against checkpoints, and both can revise the original plan a second time; whether and when to revise depends more on the cost of the change, who is waiting on the result and how the contract is written.
